passages.text:
Clement to James, the lord and bishop of bishops, who governs the holy Jerusalem church of the Hebrews and the churches everywhere that have been well established by God’s providence, together with the elders and deacons and all the other brothers: may peace always be.

Let it be known to you, my lord, that Simon—who, because of his true faith and the most secure basis of his teaching, was designated to be the foundation of the church and, for this very reason, was renamed Peter by Jesus himself with his unlying mouth; the firstfruits of our Lord; the first of the apostles; the one to whom the Father first revealed the Son; the one whom the Messiah rightly pronounced blessed; the called and chosen one, table companion and fellow traveler; the good and proven disciple; the one commanded to illuminate the West, the darker part of the world, as more capable than everyone else, and who proved able to accomplish it; and indeed, how long shall I prolong the account, unwilling to disclose the painful thing that necessity compels me, even if late, in any event to tell?—this same man, because of his boundless affection for humanity, having clearly and publicly proclaimed to the whole world, under the present evil one, the future good king, and having come as far as here, to Rome, saving people through teaching willed by God, himself left this present life through violence.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ δὴ μέχρι ποῦ· μηκύνω τὸν λόγον, μὴ βουλόμενος σημῆναι τὸ λυποῦν, ὃ ἐξ ἀνάγκης κἂν βραδὺ πάντως εἰπεῖν με δεῖ;
source_issues.issue: The printed high point after μέχρι ποῦ interrupts the interrogative phrase from its verb μηκύνω, leaving the exact scope of the rhetorical question editorially uncertain. The translation provisionally takes the words together as a rhetorical interruption within the larger sentence about Simon; the punctuation is a confirmed editorial feature, not evidence of source corruption.
source_issues.proposed_reading: καὶ δὴ μέχρι ποῦ μηκύνω τὸν λόγον, μὴ βουλόμενος σημῆναι τὸ λυποῦν, ὃ ἐξ ἀνάγκης κἂν βραδὺ πάντως εἰπεῖν με δεῖ;

lexical_decisions.chosen: the holy Jerusalem church of the Hebrews
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves Jerusalem as the church’s location or identifying designation and retains its explicit association with the Hebrews.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν ἀσφαλεστάτην αὐτοῦ τῆς διδασκαλίας ὑπόθεσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: the most secure basis of his teaching
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders ὑπόθεσις as the underlying basis of the teaching and preserves the superlative force of ἀσφαλεστάτην.

lexical_decisions.chosen: with his unlying mouth
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the source’s concrete image and its claim that Jesus’ naming was free from falsehood.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: Χριστός functions independently as a title here rather than as part of the name Jesus Christ.

lexical_decisions.chosen: this same man
lexical_decisions.rationale: Marks the emphatic resumption of Simon after the extended series of descriptions and the intervening rhetorical question.

lexical_decisions.chosen: under the present evil one
lexical_decisions.rationale: With the genitive, ἐπί is taken temporally as locating the proclamation under the ascendancy of a personal evil figure; a more impersonal reading, ‘amid the present evil,’ remains possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: through teaching willed by God
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders θεοβούλητος as describing teaching that accords with or proceeds from God’s will.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ νῦν βίου βιαίως τὸ ζῆν μετήλλαξεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: left this present life through violence
lexical_decisions.rationale: Communicates the death denoted by the exchange-language while retaining the explicit claim that the departure from life was violent; μετήλλαξεν literally depicts an exchange or change, without naming what was received in exchange.

passages.text: Now, in the very days when he was about to die, after the brothers had assembled, he suddenly took hold of my hand, stood up before the church, and said, “Listen to me, brothers and fellow servants. Since—as I was taught by the Lord and Teacher Jesus Christ, who sent me—the days of my death have drawn near, I ordain this Clement as bishop for you. To him I entrust my chair of teaching. He accompanied me from the beginning to the end and thus listened to all my discourses; to speak in summary, he shared in all my trials and was found persevering in faith. More than anyone else, I have found by experience that he is God-revering, a lover of humanity, pure, widely learned, self-controlled, good, just, patient, and knows how to bear bravely the acts of ingratitude committed by some of those receiving instruction. Therefore I impart to him the authority to bind and release, so that, concerning whatever he ordains on earth, it will stand decreed in the heavens. For he will bind what must be bound and release what must be released, since he knows the church’s rule. Listen to him, therefore, recognizing that whoever grieves the one who presides over truth sins against the Messiah and provokes the Father of all; for this reason, that person will not live. Therefore the one who presides must himself occupy the place of a physician, not possess the rage of an irrational beast.”

source_issues.source_quote: ἵνα περὶ παντὸς οὗ ἂν χειροτονήσῃ ἐπὶ γῆς ἔσται δεδογματισμένον ἐν οὐρανοῖς
source_issues.issue: The gender and reference of παντὸς οὗ and the semantic range of χειροτονέω permit both an impersonal interpretation, ‘concerning whatever he ordains on earth,’ and a personal interpretation, ‘concerning anyone he appoints on earth.’ The main translation provisionally adopts the former while preserving περὶ and the recurrence of the ordination verb; neither interpretation is uniquely established by the supplied wording.

lexical_decisions.chosen: fellow servants
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the shared servant status expressed by the compound rather than reducing it to a general term for colleagues.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ᾧ τὴν ἐμὴν τῶν λόγων πιστεύω καθέδραν
lexical_decisions.chosen: To him I entrust my chair of teaching
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the institutional chair image while taking τῶν λόγων to characterize it as the chair associated with Peter’s words or teaching.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to speak in summary
lexical_decisions.rationale: Conveys the idiom’s transition from the preceding details to a concise characterization.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a lover of humanity
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the word’s explicit orientation toward human beings rather than narrowing it to generic kindness.

lexical_decisions.chosen: those receiving instruction
lexical_decisions.rationale: Conveys the participle’s sense without requiring the later technical loanword ‘catechumens.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: to bind and release
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the paired judicial and disciplinary imagery while distinguishing λύειν from merely untying a physical object.

lexical_decisions.chosen: concerning whatever he ordains
lexical_decisions.rationale: Restores the explicit περὶ, ‘concerning,’ and keeps χειροτονέω visibly connected with the earlier ‘I ordain.’ The phrase may instead refer personally to ‘anyone he appoints.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: it will stand decreed in the heavens
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the established-decree sense of δεδογματισμένον without directly identifying the object of Clement’s earthly action with the heavenly decree.

lexical_decisions.chosen: occupy the place of a physician
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the contrast between healing authority and the rage of an irrational beast.

passages.text: As he was saying these things, I fell before him and pleaded with him, declining the honor and authority of the chair. But he answered, “Do not ask this of me, for I have resolved that this should happen—and all the more for this very reason, if you decline it—because such a chair does not need a rash man eager to occupy the chair, but one who is circumspect in character and widely learned in discourse. Produce someone better, one who accompanied me more than you, listened to my words, and thoroughly learned the governance of the church, and I will not force you, against your will, to do what is right. But you will not now be able to produce anyone better than yourself, for you are the superior firstfruit of the nations being saved through me. Nevertheless, consider this other point as well: if, fearing the danger of sin, you do not undertake the governance of the church, know well that you sin more, since, though able to help those who revere God, as people sailing and in danger, you refuse, considering only your own interest and not what benefits everyone in common. I understand correctly that you must, in any event, undertake the danger, since I do not cease asking this of you for the help of everyone. Therefore, the sooner you agree with me, the more you will relieve me of discouragement.”

source_issues.source_quote: ὁ δ᾽. ἀπεκρίνατο
source_issues.issue: The supplied print places a full stop immediately after the elided δ᾽, syntactically separating ὁ δ᾽ from ἀπεκρίνατο. The translation provisionally reads the words continuously as ‘But he answered.’ This appears to be an editorial punctuation blemish, not evidence of missing text.

source_issues.source_quote: σὺ γὰρ δι᾽ ἐμοῦ τῶν σωζομένων ἐθνῶν ἡ κρείττων ἀπαρχή
source_issues.issue: The attachment of δι᾽ ἐμοῦ is interpretively uncertain. The translation connects it with σωζομένων, yielding ‘the nations being saved through me.’ It can instead modify the main assertion: ‘through me you are the superior firstfruit of the nations being saved.’ The supplied wording requires no textual correction.

source_issues.source_quote: σὺ γὰρ δι᾽ ἐμοῦ τῶν σωζομένων ἐθνῶν ἡ κρείττων ἀπαρχή
source_issues.issue: The plural ἐθνῶν can refer to nations as collective populations or to Gentile persons. The latter is especially relevant because Clement is described individually as a firstfruit. The main wording retains “nations”; “the Gentiles who are being saved” is a viable alternative, alongside the separately disclosed ambiguity in the attachment of δι᾽ ἐμοῦ. This is interpretive uncertainty, not a proposed correction to the Greek.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: παραιτούμενος τὴν τῆς καθέδρας τιμήν τε καὶ ἐξουσίαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: declining the honor and authority of the chair
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves Clement’s refusal of both the office’s honor and its governing power.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a rash man eager to occupy the chair
lexical_decisions.rationale: Conveys the coined expression’s criticism of someone recklessly ambitious for the presiding seat.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εὐλαβοῦς τὸν τρόπον καὶ πολυμαθοῦς τὸν λόγον
lexical_decisions.chosen: circumspect in character and widely learned in discourse
lexical_decisions.rationale: The context contrasts reckless ambition with cautious character and extensive competence in teaching or discourse.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Produce someone better
lexical_decisions.rationale: The imperative challenges Clement to supply a more qualified alternative, continuing the comparative language of κρείττων.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the superior firstfruit
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains κρείττων as a comparative description rather than converting it into an English superlative; ‘more excellent firstfruit’ is a possible alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: as people sailing and in danger
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains both the maritime action and the accompanying danger.

lexical_decisions.chosen: what benefits everyone in common
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the contrast between Clement’s private interest and the community’s shared good.

lexical_decisions.chosen: you agree with me
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compound describes Clement joining Peter in approving and accepting the proposed course.

passages.text: “And I myself also know, Clement, that I am bestowing on you griefs, discouragements, dangers, and reproaches from uneducated crowds. You will be able to bear these bravely by keeping in view the great reward from God that will be paid to you for your endurance. But also, as is right, consider together with me: when does the Messiah need your alliance—now, when the evil one has taken up war against his bride, or in the coming time, when, having conquered, he reigns and no longer needs any help? Is it not clear even to someone with little understanding that it is now? Therefore, with full resolve, hurry in this present time of need to ally yourself with a good king, whose nature it is to pay great rewards after victory. Gladly, then, exercise oversight—all the more suitably in this respect, since you have learned from me how to govern the church—for the salvation of the brothers who flee to us for refuge.”

source_issues.source_quote: μισθοὺς μεγάλους· μετὰ νίκην ἀποδιδόναι πεφυκότι
source_issues.issue: The printed high point places a strong editorial pause between the object μισθοὺς μεγάλους and the infinitive ἀποδιδόναι on which it depends. The syntax remains recoverable, and the translation provisionally reads the phrase continuously. The proposed reading is conjectural repunctuation only.
source_issues.proposed_reading: μισθοὺς μεγάλους μετὰ νίκην ἀποδιδόναι πεφυκότι

lexical_decisions.chosen: I am bestowing on you
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses a single gift-related verb for Peter’s act and keeps the griefs, dangers, and reproaches as its objects; the verb pointedly presents the imposed burdens as things bestowed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐνορῶν τῆς ὑπομονῆς τὸν ἐκ θεοῦ σοι μέγαν ἀποδιδόμενον μισθόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: keeping in view the great reward from God that will be paid to you for your endurance
lexical_decisions.rationale: With rewards as its object, ἀποδίδωμι denotes paying the recompense owed, not returning a reward previously received. The repeated English payment wording preserves the recurrence without suggesting an earlier payment.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: Χριστός functions independently as the title of the king whose cause Clement is urged to support.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κατὰ τῆς αὐτοῦ νύμφης πόλεμον ἤρατο
lexical_decisions.chosen: has taken up war against his bride
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps both the military action and the bride image without identifying the bride more explicitly than the source does.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Therefore, with full resolve
lexical_decisions.rationale: Προαίρεσις denotes deliberate purpose or resolve, while πάσῃ supplies the comprehensive force represented by ‘full.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: to ally yourself with a good king
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the political and military alliance imagery rather than generalizing it as mere assistance.

lexical_decisions.chosen: whose nature it is to pay
lexical_decisions.rationale: With rewards as its object, ἀποδίδωμι denotes paying the recompense owed, not returning a reward previously received. The repeated English payment wording preserves the recurrence without suggesting an earlier payment.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Gladly, then, exercise oversight
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb calls Clement to perform episcopal oversight and retains its word-family connection with ἐπίσκοπος without forcing an English denominational formulation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the brothers who flee to us for refuge
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the directional movement and protective force of προσφεύγω.

passages.text: “Nevertheless, before everyone and for everyone’s sake, I also wish to remind you briefly about the matters of governance. You must live blamelessly and, with the greatest diligence, shake off all the occupations of life, becoming neither a guarantor nor an advocate and becoming entangled in no other worldly affair. For the Messiah does not want you appointed as a judge and adjudicator over money or business among the present affairs of worldly life and thereby, absorbed in people’s present concerns, left without leisure to separate, by the word of truth, the better people from the worse. Rather, let those who are learning provide these things for one another, and let them not distract you from the words capable of saving. For just as it is impious for you to undertake worldly concerns while neglecting to do what you were commanded, so it is a sin for each layperson if they do not stand by one another also in worldly needs. Moreover, if all of them do not understand about which matters they ought to keep you free from concern, let them learn from the deacons, so that you may care only for the church, both governing it well and providing the words of truth.”

source_issues.source_quote: οὐ γὰρ κριτὴν καὶ δικαστὴν χρημάτων ἢ ἀσχολημάτων καθεστάναι σε θέλει τῶν νῦν βιωτικῶν πραγμάτων ὁ χριστός, ἵνα συνεχόμενος εἰς τὰς νῦν τῶν ἀνθρώπων φροντίδας μὴ εὐσχολῇς χωρίζειν λόγῳ ἀληθείας ἀνθρώπων τοὺς κρείττονας ἀπὸ τῶν χειρόνων
source_issues.issue: The scope of the unusual οὐ ... θέλει ... ἵνα ... μὴ construction is interpretively difficult. The translation takes the ἵνα clause as the unwanted outcome included within the Messiah’s negated desire: appointment to worldly adjudication would absorb Clement and leave him without leisure for his teaching task. A more formally sequential rendering with ‘so that’ could obscure this scope or suggest that the lack of leisure is the purpose of refusing the appointment. No textual correction is proposed.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ σὲ δὲ περὶ ὧν χρὴ ἀμέριμνον εἶναι οἱ πάντες ποιεῖν ἐὰν μὴ νοῶσιν, παρὰ τῶν διακόνων μανθανέτωσαν
source_issues.issue: The marked word order leaves the relationship of χρὴ to ἀμέριμνον εἶναι and ποιεῖν interpretively uncertain. The translation provisionally understands the necessity as governing the community’s keeping Clement free from concern about certain matters. Alternatively, the phrase may mean that Clement himself ought to be free from concern about those matters and that, if all do not know how to make him so, they should learn from the deacons. This is a syntactic ambiguity in the supplied wording, not evidence of missing or corrupt text.

lexical_decisions.chosen: before everyone and for everyone’s sake
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes ἐπὶ πάντων as indicating the public setting and διὰ πάντας as expressing the concern for everyone that motivates the instruction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πάσας τὰς τοῦ βίου ἀσχολίας ἀποσείεσθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: shake off all the occupations of life
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the physical force of ἀποσείω and the comprehensive scope of πάσας.

lexical_decisions.chosen: becoming neither a guarantor nor an advocate
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the distinct financial and legal roles prohibited to the bishop.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κριτὴν καὶ δικαστὴν χρημάτων ἢ ἀσχολημάτων
lexical_decisions.chosen: a judge and adjudicator over money or business
lexical_decisions.rationale: Distinguishes the two judicial terms while treating χρημάτων and ἀσχολημάτων as the financial and business matters over which judgment would be exercised.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: χωρίζειν λόγῳ ἀληθείας ἀνθρώπων τοὺς κρείττονας ἀπὸ τῶν χειρόνων
lexical_decisions.chosen: to separate, by the word of truth, the better people from the worse
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the source’s language of separation and its comparison between better and worse persons.

lexical_decisions.chosen: those who are learning
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the expression broader than a fixed institutional label such as ‘catechumens.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: for each layperson
lexical_decisions.rationale: Λαϊκός distinguishes an ordinary member from the bishop and deacons in the surrounding instructions.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: περὶ ὧν χρὴ ἀμέριμνον εἶναι οἱ πάντες ποιεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: about which matters they ought to keep you free from concern
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the freedom specifically as freedom from concern about the matters, not freedom from the matters themselves. The placement of χρὴ also permits taking the necessity as applying directly to Clement’s being free from concern.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μόνης τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὴν φροντίδα ἔχῃς
lexical_decisions.chosen: you may care only for the church
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the exclusive force of μόνης and the church as the bishop’s assigned sphere of concern.

passages.text: For if you become occupied with the cares of ordinary life, you will lay an ambush for both yourself and your hearers. For because your occupations leave you unable to furnish what is beneficial as provisions, you will be punished for not teaching what is beneficial, while those who did not learn will perish, ignorance being the cause. Therefore, give them your undistracted time and preside over them, so that at the right time you may provide words capable of saving them. And so let them heed you, knowing that whatever the ambassador of the truth binds on earth has also been bound in heaven, and whatever he looses has been loosed. You, however, will bind what must be bound and loose what must be loosed. And as for the matters concerning you, the presiding officer, these are they, along with things like them.

source_issues.source_quote: οἱ δὲ μὴ μαθόντες ἀγνοίας αἰτία ἀπολοῦνται
source_issues.issue: The printed nominative αἰτία is syntactically abrupt. The translation understands it parenthetically as “ignorance being the cause”; a causal dative is a possible conjecture, but the supplied reading has not been replaced.
source_issues.proposed_reading: οἱ δὲ μὴ μαθόντες ἀγνοίας αἰτίᾳ ἀπολοῦνται

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ τὰ μὲν. κατὰ σὲ
source_issues.issue: The printed full stop interrupts the construction and separates μὲν from the phrase it appears to qualify. The translation reads the words as continuous in sense without treating the supplied punctuation as a transcription error.

lexical_decisions.chosen: become occupied with the cares of ordinary life
lexical_decisions.rationale: βιωτικός concerns ordinary worldly life, while ἀσχολέομαι emphasizes being occupied and deprived of leisure.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ σεαυτὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀκροατὰς ἐνεδρεύσεις
lexical_decisions.chosen: you will lay an ambush for both yourself and your hearers
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐνεδρεύω specifically evokes lying in ambush; the image is retained rather than generalized as merely endangering or ensnaring.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to furnish what is beneficial as provisions
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐφοδιάζω evokes supplying provisions or equipping someone for a journey.

lexical_decisions.chosen: give them your undistracted time and preside over them
lexical_decisions.rationale: εὐσχολέω contrasts with prior preoccupation, while προκαθέζομαι denotes taking the leading or presiding position.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁ τῆς ἀληθείας πρεσβευτὴς ὃ ἂν δήσῃ ἐπὶ γῆς, δέδεται καὶ ἐν οὐρανῷ
lexical_decisions.chosen: whatever the ambassador of the truth binds on earth has also been bound in heaven
lexical_decisions.rationale: πρεσβευτής denotes an authorized envoy, and the Greek perfect is retained rather than harmonized with a familiar future-tense rendering.

passages.text: But let the duties concerning the elders be these: above all, let them quickly join the young in marriage, forestalling the snares of youthful desire. But let them not neglect marriage even for those already old, for in some people desire remains vigorous even after they have grown old. Therefore, so that sexual immorality may not gain ground against you and cast the same plague into your midst, take precautions beforehand and investigate whether the fire of adultery may be springing up secretly among you. For adultery is exceedingly terrible—so much so that it holds second place in punishment, since first place is awarded to those who are in error, even if they are chaste. Therefore, as elders of the church, train the Messiah’s bride in chastity (and by “bride” I mean the corporate body of the church). For if she is found chaste by the bridegroom king, she will obtain the greatest honor, and you, as those invited to the wedding, will enjoy great rejoicing. But if she is discovered to have sinned, she will be cast out, and you will pay the penalty—lest perhaps the sin have come about through your neglect.

source_issues.source_quote: ὑμεῖς δὲ δίκην δώσετε μήπως παρὰ τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀμέλειαν γέγονεν ἡ ἁμαρτία
source_issues.issue: The dependency and force of μήπως are uncertain. It may have an apprehensive sense, “lest perhaps,” as translated, or introduce something closer to “whether perhaps”; taking it as “if perhaps” would make payment of the penalty conditional on negligence. The explicit assertion δίκην δώσετε remains independent in the translation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πρὸ πάντων τοὺς νέους πρὸς γάμον ζευγνύτωσαν ἐν τάχει
lexical_decisions.chosen: above all, let them quickly join the young in marriage
lexical_decisions.rationale: ζευγνύω literally joins or yokes together and here refers to arranging marriage.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the snares of youthful desire
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves the trapping image of παγίδευμα and treats νεάζουσα as characterizing desire associated with youth.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ πορνεία νομὴν λαβοῦσα καθ’ ὑμῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: sexual immorality may not gain ground against you
lexical_decisions.rationale: νομὴν λαμβάνειν can describe spreading or gaining range, especially of disease or fire.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοσοῦτον ὅσον τὰ δευτερεῖα ἔχειν αὐτὴν τῆς κολάσεως
lexical_decisions.chosen: so much so that it holds second place in punishment
lexical_decisions.rationale: δευτερεῖα denotes second rank or second prize; the ranking image is retained.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐπεὶ τὰ πρωτεῖα τοῖς ἐν πλάνῃ οὖσιν ἀποδίδοται, κἂν σωφρονῶσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: since first place is awarded to those who are in error, even if they are chaste
lexical_decisions.rationale: πλάνη may denote doctrinal or moral error, but the text does not specify further; the surprising concession about chastity is preserved.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐξασκήσατε τὴν χριστοῦ νύμφην εἰς σωφροσύνην
lexical_decisions.chosen: train the Messiah’s bride in chastity
lexical_decisions.rationale: χριστοῦ stands independently as a designation and is therefore rendered titularly as “the Messiah’s,” while ἐξασκέω conveys disciplined training or cultivation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: νύμφην δὲ λέγω τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὸ σύστημα
lexical_decisions.chosen: and by “bride” I mean the corporate body of the church
lexical_decisions.rationale: σύστημα denotes an organized whole or collective body.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑμεῖς δὲ δίκην δώσετε μήπως παρὰ τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀμέλειαν γέγονεν ἡ ἁμαρτία
lexical_decisions.chosen: and you will pay the penalty—lest perhaps the sin have come about through your neglect
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves the explicit future statement δίκην δώσετε and represents μήπως apprehensively rather than converting the entire statement into an unmarked conditional.

passages.text: Therefore, above all, concern yourselves with chastity, for sexual immorality has been decreed exceedingly grave in God’s sight. There are many kinds of sexual immorality, as Clement himself will also explain to you. But the first is adultery: a man’s not having relations only with his own wife, and a woman’s not having relations only with her own husband. If someone is chaste, he can also come to love humanity, for which reason he will obtain eternal mercy. Just as adultery is a great evil, so love for humanity is the greatest good. Therefore love all your brothers with reverent and merciful eyes, doing for orphans what parents do and for widows what husbands do, providing sustenance with complete gladness, marriages for those in their prime, and, for those among them without a trade, devising through occupations the means of necessary sustenance: work for a craftsperson, mercy for someone unable to work.

source_issues.source_quote: πλὴν πρώτη μοιχεία ἐστὶν τὸ ἄνδρα μὴ ἰδίᾳ μόνῃ χρήσασθαι γυναικὶ καὶ γυναῖκα μὴ ἰδίῳ μόνῳ χρήσασθαι ἀνδρί.
source_issues.issue: The translation takes πρώτη elliptically as marking adultery as the first of the previously mentioned kinds of sexual immorality. Since πρώτη is feminine and agrees directly with μοιχεία rather than with the neuter plural εἴδη, the construction may instead mean, “But the first,” or “primary, form of adultery consists in a man’s not having relations only with his own wife and a woman’s not having relations only with her own husband.” This is an interpretive uncertainty, not evidence that the supplied Greek is defective.

source_issues.source_quote: τεχνίτῃ ἔργον, ἀδρανεῖ ἔλεος.
source_issues.issue: In this contrast, ἀδρανεῖ may refer to someone weak or unable to work, as the translation provisionally understands it, but it can also designate someone inactive or idle. The compressed wording does not make the reason for the person’s inactivity explicit.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: λίαν γὰρ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ χαλεπὴ ὥρισται ἡ πορνεία
lexical_decisions.chosen: sexual immorality has been decreed exceedingly grave in God’s sight
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὁρίζω indicates authoritative determination, while χαλεπή here describes severity or gravity.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πορνείας δὲ εἴδη πολλά, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς Κλήμης ὑμῖν διηγήσεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: There are many kinds of sexual immorality, as Clement himself will also explain to you
lexical_decisions.rationale: The translation preserves καί, which marks Clement himself as also supplying the promised explanation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: But the first is adultery
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main rendering takes πρώτη elliptically as introducing the first of the kinds just mentioned. Because πρώτη is feminine and directly agrees with μοιχεία, the alternative sense “the first” or “primary adultery” remains possible and is disclosed separately.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ ἄνδρα μὴ ἰδίᾳ μόνῃ χρήσασθαι γυναικὶ καὶ γυναῖκα μὴ ἰδίῳ μόνῳ χρήσασθαι ἀνδρί
lexical_decisions.chosen: a man’s not having relations only with his own wife, and a woman’s not having relations only with her own husband
lexical_decisions.rationale: χρῆσθαι with a spouse in this context refers to sexual or marital relations; a literal rendering with “use” would mislead.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐὰν σώφρων ᾖ τις, καὶ φιλάνθρωπος γενέσθαι δύναται
lexical_decisions.chosen: If someone is chaste, he can also come to love humanity
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verbal English represents φιλάνθρωπος as an orientation of love toward humanity and keeps its human referent visible for consistency with the cognate noun.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς δὲ ἡ μοιχεία μέγα κακόν, οὕτως ἡ φιλανθρωπία μέγιστον ἀγαθόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Just as adultery is a great evil, so love for humanity is the greatest good
lexical_decisions.rationale: “Love for humanity” makes the components and human referent of φιλανθρωπία visible and supports the explicit contrast with μισανθρωπία in the following section.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῖς αὐτῶν ἀτέχνοις διὰ τῶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων ἐννοούμενοι τὰς προφάσεις τῆς ἀναγκαίας τροφῆς
lexical_decisions.chosen: for those among them without a trade, devising through occupations the means of necessary sustenance
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀτέχνοις is taken as “unskilled” or “without a trade,” while προφάσεις denotes practical occasions or means in this context.

lexical_decisions.chosen: work for a craftsperson, mercy for someone unable to work
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compressed contrast assigns work to the craftsperson and charitable aid to the ἀδρανής person. In context, the latter may be someone weak or unable to work, though the term can also mean inactive or idle; the English follows the incapacity reading without making it lexically certain.

passages.text: I know that you will do these things if you establish love in your mind. There is one sufficient occasion for its entry: the common sharing of salt. Therefore make every effort to dine with one another more frequently, as you are able, so that you do not barter it away; for it is the cause of doing good, and doing good is the cause of salvation. All of you, then, make your means of life common to everyone who is a brother according to God, knowing that by giving temporary things you will receive eternal things. All the more, feed the hungry and provide drink to the thirsty, clothing to the naked; visit the sick; make yourselves present to those in prison and help them as you can; receive strangers into your own homes with complete eagerness. But, so that I do not speak item by item, love for humanity will teach you to do every good thing, just as hatred of humanity points out the practice of evil to those who do not wish to be saved.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ διψῶσι παρέχετε· ποτόν
source_issues.issue: The printed middle dot separates παρέχετε from ποτόν even though “drink” naturally serves as its object. The translation construes them together while disclosing the punctuation as supplied.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μία τις ἐστὶν ἱκανὴ πρόφασις, ἡ κοινὴ τῶν ἁλῶν μετάληψις
lexical_decisions.chosen: There is one sufficient occasion for its entry: the common sharing of salt
lexical_decisions.rationale: πρόφασις here denotes an occasion or means, while the specific salt image evokes shared food and table fellowship.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: σπουδάζετε πυκνότερον συνέστιοι ἀλλήλων γίνεσθαι ὡς δύνασθε
lexical_decisions.chosen: make every effort to dine with one another more frequently, as you are able
lexical_decisions.rationale: σύνεστιος describes sharing a table or household meal; “more frequently” preserves the comparative πυκνότερον separately from the qualification of ability expressed by ὡς δύνασθε.

lexical_decisions.chosen: so that you do not barter it away
lexical_decisions.rationale: The pronoun refers to love, and ἀπεμπολέω supplies a commercial image of selling or trading something away.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κοινοὺς οὖν πάντες πᾶσιν τοῖς κατὰ θεὸν ἀδελφοῖς τοὺς ἑαυτῶν παρέχετε βίους
lexical_decisions.chosen: All of you, then, make your means of life common to everyone who is a brother according to God
lexical_decisions.rationale: βίος can denote life, livelihood, or material means; the giving context favors “means of life” while retaining more breadth than “money.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῖς ἐν φυλακαῖς ἐπιφαινόμενοι ὡς δύνασθε βοηθεῖτε
lexical_decisions.chosen: make yourselves present to those in prison and help them as you can
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπιφαίνομαι literally denotes appearing or making oneself visible, here in the practical sense of visiting or being present.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ τὸ κατ᾽ εἶδος λέγω
lexical_decisions.chosen: so that I do not speak item by item
lexical_decisions.rationale: κατ᾽ εἶδος here means treating each matter separately by kind or category.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πᾶν καλὸν ἡ φιλανθρωπία ὑμᾶς ποιεῖν διδάξει, ὥσπερ ἡ μισανθρωπία τοῖς μὴ βουλομένοις σώζεσθαι τὴν κακοπραξίαν ὑποδείκνυσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: love for humanity will teach you to do every good thing, just as hatred of humanity points out the practice of evil to those who do not wish to be saved
lexical_decisions.rationale: The matched phrases “love for humanity” and “hatred of humanity” preserve the explicit human referent and the lexical antithesis between φιλανθρωπία and μισανθρωπία.

passages.text: Brothers who have disputes must not have their cases judged before the authorities, but must in every way be brought to agreement by the elders of the church, readily obeying them. Moreover, flee greed as something capable, under the pretext of temporary gain, of depriving you of eternal good things. Do you carefully observe balances, measures, and weights—the lawful standards of the localities? Act honorably with regard to deposits entrusted to you. Moreover, you will persevere in doing these and similar things to the end if you keep in your hearts an inseparable remembrance of the judgment that comes from God. For who could sin while fully convinced that judgment from the righteous God—who alone is now patient and good—has been appointed to take place at the completion of life, so that the good may thereafter enjoy the inexpressible good things everlastingly, while those found to be sinners, as evil people, will receive inexpressible punishment forever? And as for these things being so, if the prophet of the truth had not stated under oath that they would be, it might perhaps have been reasonable to doubt.

source_issues.source_quote: τῶντόπων
source_issues.issue: The supplied print joins the article and noun without a space. This is an orthographic word-division feature and does not by itself create substantive uncertainty.

source_issues.source_quote: ζυγά, μέτρα, σταθμία, τὰ τῶντόπων δίκαια ἐπιμελῶς φυλάσσετε;
source_issues.issue: The supplied punctuation presents the sentence as a question, although φυλάσσετε can formally be read as either indicative or imperative. The translation retains the question. Syntactically, τὰ τῶντόπων δίκαια may appositionally identify the preceding balances, measures, and weights as the lawful local standards, as translated, or it may be a separate fourth object referring more generally to the lawful requirements of the localities.

source_issues.source_quote: τοῦ νῦν μόνου μακροθύμου καὶ ἀγαθοῦ
source_issues.issue: The translation takes μόνου as person-exclusive: “the righteous God, who alone is now patient and good.” Its agreement with the reference to God supports that reading. In view of the contrast between God’s present patience and the coming judgment, a less straightforward present-mode interpretation is also possible: “who is now only patient and good.” That alternative does not mean “only for now,” which could imply that the attributes themselves will cease, and it would more normally be expressed with an adverb such as μόνον. The supplied μόνου has therefore not been altered.

source_issues.source_quote: ἵνα οἱ ἀγαθοὶ τοῦ λοιποῦ τῶν ἀπορρήτων ἀγαθῶν ἀιδίως ἀπολαύσωσιν, οἱ δὲ ἁμαρτωλοὶ εὑρεθέντες ὡς κακοὶ ἀπορρήτου κολάσεως τεύξονται τὸν αἰῶνα
source_issues.issue: Within the result clause introduced by ἵνα, the first outcome uses the subjunctive ἀπολαύσωσιν, while the second shifts to the future indicative τεύξονται. The translation treats them as coordinated outcomes without correcting the grammatical shift.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Brothers who have disputes
lexical_decisions.rationale: πράγματα ἔχειν in this legal setting refers to having cases, grievances, or disputes.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑπὸ τῶν τῆς ἐκκλησίας πρεσβυτέρων συμβιβαζέσθωσαν παντὶ τρόπῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: must in every way be brought to agreement by the elders of the church
lexical_decisions.rationale: συμβιβάζω here concerns reconciling the parties or settling their dispute.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πλὴν καὶ τὴν πλεονεξίαν οὕτως φεύγετε ὡς προφάσει προσκαίρου κέρδους ἀπὸ τῶν αἰωνίων ἀγαθῶν ζημιοῦν δυναμένην
lexical_decisions.chosen: Moreover, flee greed as something capable, under the pretext of temporary gain, of depriving you of eternal good things
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves greed as the feminine referent of δυναμένην and retains the contrast between temporary gain and loss of eternal goods.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ζυγά, μέτρα, σταθμία, τὰ τῶντόπων δίκαια ἐπιμελῶς φυλάσσετε;
lexical_decisions.chosen: Do you carefully observe balances, measures, and weights—the lawful standards of the localities?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied question punctuation is retained. The neuter phrase τὰ τῶντόπων δίκαια is construed appositionally as identifying the preceding balances, measures, and weights as the locally lawful standards.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Act honorably with regard to deposits entrusted to you
lexical_decisions.rationale: With entrusted property, εὐγνωμονέω denotes conscientious, fair, or honorable conduct rather than simple gratitude.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ νῦν μόνου μακροθύμου καὶ ἀγαθοῦ
lexical_decisions.chosen: who alone is now patient and good
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main rendering follows the straightforward person-exclusive reading, taking μόνου as agreeing with the reference to God. The context’s contrast between present patience and ensuing judgment also creates some pressure toward the less direct present-mode sense “who is now only patient and good”; that alternative is disclosed without changing μόνου to an adverb.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῶν ἀπορρήτων ἀγαθῶν ἀιδίως ἀπολαύσωσιν, οἱ δὲ ἁμαρτωλοὶ εὑρεθέντες ὡς κακοὶ ἀπορρήτου κολάσεως τεύξονται τὸν αἰῶνα
lexical_decisions.chosen: enjoy the inexpressible good things everlastingly, while those found to be sinners, as evil people, will receive inexpressible punishment forever
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀπόρρητος is rendered consistently on both sides. The different temporal expressions remain visible as “everlastingly” for ἀιδίως and “forever” for the idiomatic τὸν αἰῶνα; the latter is literally “for the age” or “throughout the age,” but the change of expression does not by itself establish different durations.

passages.text: Therefore, since you truly are disciples of a prophet, lay aside the discord from which wrongdoing arises and eagerly undertake to do good. But if any of you doubts that what has been said will happen, let him admit it without shame, provided that he cares for his own soul, and he will be fully assured by the one who presides. But if he has believed rightly, let him confidently conduct his life as one fleeing a great fire of condemnation and entering God’s everlasting, good kingdom.

lexical_decisions.chosen: since you truly are disciples of a prophet
lexical_decisions.rationale: Leaves the prophet unnamed and preserves the emphasis that the addressees truly are his disciples.

lexical_decisions.chosen: eagerly undertake to do good
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders ἀναδέξασθε as willingly taking up a responsibility rather than merely beginning an action.

lexical_decisions.chosen: he will be fully assured by the one who presides
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the passive sense of receiving assurance and does not import a more specific ecclesiastical title.

lexical_decisions.chosen: let him confidently conduct his life
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes πολιτεύεσθαι as living or conducting oneself, with θαρρῶν supplying confidence.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς ἀιδίαν ἀγαθὴν θεοῦ βασιλείαν εἰσερχόμενος
lexical_decisions.chosen: entering God’s everlasting, good kingdom
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both adjectives applied to the kingdom and its attribution to God.

passages.text: Those who catechize should first be catechized and then catechize, for the work concerns the human soul. For the instructor in the discourses must adapt himself to the many dispositions of those who are learning. The one who catechizes must therefore be widely learned, above reproach, highly experienced, and fearless, as you yourselves will find Clement—who is to catechize after me—to be. For it would take too long for me now to discuss the matter item by item. Nevertheless, if you are of one mind, you will be able to be carried into the harbor of rest, where there is the peaceful city of a great king.

source_issues.source_quote: κατηχήθέντες
source_issues.issue: The selected source writes two acute accents in κατηχήθέντες. Its identification as a passive participle is clear. This is disclosed as a supplied orthographic feature, not as missing wording or an established OCR error; the source is not silently normalized.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Those who catechize should first be catechized and then catechize
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the repeated κατηχέω word family and the required sequence of first receiving and then giving instruction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅτι περὶ ψυχῆς ἀνθρώπων τὸ ἔργον
lexical_decisions.chosen: for the work concerns human souls
lexical_decisions.rationale: Expresses the compressed singular Greek phrase idiomatically without diminishing its concern for the souls of human beings.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πρὸς γὰρ τὰς πολλὰς τῶν μανθανόντων γνώμας συναρμόζεσθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: must adapt himself to the many dispositions of those who are learning
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes γνώμαι as the varied dispositions or outlooks of learners and συναρμόζεσθαι as adapting instruction accordingly.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πολὺ γὰρ ἐστὶν ἐμὲ νῦν τὸ κατ’ εἶδος λέγειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: For it would take too long for me now to discuss the matter item by item
lexical_decisions.rationale: Understands κατ’ εἶδος as detailed treatment according to each particular and πολὺ as indicating that such treatment would be extensive.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς τὸν τῆς ἀναπαύσεως ἐνεχθῆναι λιμένα
lexical_decisions.chosen: to be carried into the harbor of rest
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the passive nautical image that introduces the extended ship allegory of the following sections.

passages.text: For the whole enterprise of the church resembles a large ship carrying through a fierce storm men who are from many places and who wish to inhabit one particular city belonging to a good kingdom. Let God, then, be the master of this ship for you, and let the helmsman be likened to the Messiah, the bow officer to the bishop, the sailors to the elders, the officers of the ship’s sides to the deacons, the ship’s recruiters to those who catechize, the multitude of the brothers to the passengers, the world to the deep sea, and the contrary winds to the temptations. Let the persecutions, dangers, and afflictions of every kind be likened to the towering waves; the offshore winds of the torrents and the gusts to the discourses of deceivers and false prophets; the promontories and rough places to judges in positions of authority who threaten terrible things; and places between two seas and beast-infested places to those who are irrational and doubtful about the promises of the truth. Let the hypocrites be understood as likened to pirates. Nevertheless, regard sins alone as a mighty whirlpool, a Tartarean Charybdis, murderous collisions, and deadly breakups. Therefore, so that, sailing with a fair wind, you may be carried more safely into the harbor of the hoped-for city, pray so as to be heard; and prayers are heard through good deeds.

source_issues.source_quote: τὰ δὲ ἀπόγεια τῶν χειμάρρων καὶ τὰ φυσήματα
source_issues.issue: The expression is semantically compressed. ἀπόγεια can denote winds blowing from land, while τῶν χειμάρρων ordinarily means “of the torrents” or “of the winter-swollen streams.” The precise relationship of those torrents to the offshore winds is unclear. The translation preserves the supplied genitive provisionally and does not treat χειμάρρων as a form of χειμών or substitute “storms.”

source_issues.source_quote: διθάλασσοι δὲ καὶ θηριώδεις τόποι
source_issues.issue: The rendering “places between two seas” is provisional. διθάλασσος can describe exposure to sea on two sides or a meeting of two seas; the nautical-hazard context does not settle the exact configuration. This is a meaning ambiguity, not a claim of source corruption.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the whole enterprise of the church
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders πρᾶγμα broadly as the church’s entire undertaking or organized affair.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the helmsman be likened to the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the nautical office and renders independently titular χριστός as “Messiah.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁ πρωρεὺς ἐπισκόπῳ, οἱ ναῦται πρεσβυτέροις, οἱ τοίχαρχοι διακόνοις, οἱ ναυστολόγοι τοῖς κατηχοῦσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: the bow officer to the bishop, the sailors to the elders, the officers of the ship’s sides to the deacons, the ship’s recruiters to those who catechize
lexical_decisions.rationale: Maintains the differentiated shipboard roles rather than flattening them into a generic crew.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the world to the deep sea
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the grammatical direction of the comparison: the world is the subject being likened to the deep sea.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰ δὲ ἀπόγεια τῶν χειμάρρων καὶ τὰ φυσήματα
lexical_decisions.chosen: the offshore winds of the torrents and the gusts
lexical_decisions.rationale: Represents ἀπόγεια as winds blowing away from land and preserves the supplied genitive τῶν χειμάρρων rather than replacing “torrents” with “storms.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: a Tartarean Charybdis
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains both the underworld characterization and the named mythological maritime hazard.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐπηκόως εὔχεσθε· εὐχαὶ δὲ ἐπήκοοι γίνονται ταῖς εὐπραγίαις
lexical_decisions.chosen: pray so as to be heard; and prayers are heard through good deeds
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the repeated language of being heard and the author’s stated connection between heard prayer and good conduct.

passages.text: After saying these things and more than these, he again looked toward the multitude and said, “And you also, my beloved brothers and fellow servants, yield in every respect to the one presiding over truth, knowing this: whoever grieves this man has not received the Messiah, with whose chair he has been entrusted; and as one who has not received the Messiah, he will be reckoned as having rejected the Father. Therefore, he will be cast out of the good kingdom. For this reason, strive to come to every gathering, so that you may not, as deserters, incur a charge of sin because of the commander’s discouragement. Therefore, above all else, all of you should give thought to his interests, knowing that, because of each of you, the evil one wages war against him alone with greater hostility. So strive to continue in affection toward him and goodwill toward one another, and to obey him, so that he too may be relieved and you may be able to be saved.”

source_issues.source_quote: ’ὡς
source_issues.issue: The supplied print places a raised apostrophe before ὡς without an evident elision or syntactic function. Omitting it would be an orthographic normalization and would not affect the translation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: fellow servants
lexical_decisions.rationale: The term presents the brothers as sharing the status and allegiance of servants.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the one presiding over truth
lexical_decisions.rationale: The participle denotes occupying the leading seat or presiding position, with truth as its sphere.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: The first occurrence functions independently as a title.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: The second occurrence likewise functions independently as a title rather than within a personal name.

lexical_decisions.chosen: chair
lexical_decisions.rationale: The literal chair represents the entrusted teaching and governing office while preserving the source image.

lexical_decisions.chosen: deserters
lexical_decisions.rationale: This is a military term for those who abandon their assigned rank or post.

lexical_decisions.chosen: commander
lexical_decisions.rationale: The military title continues the image introduced by the reference to deserters.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to obey
lexical_decisions.rationale: In this exhortation, the verb conveys heedful compliance rather than merely hearing.

passages.text: Therefore I, my lord James, after he had said these things and I had made my promise, did not hesitate, as I had been commanded, to present in outline the greater part of the discourses from city to city, which had already been written to you beforehand and sent by him in books, as a kind of reminder, and in this form to send them to you, giving the work the title “Clement’s Epitome of Peter’s Preachings among the People.” But I will begin to set it out as I was commanded.

source_issues.source_quote: ἐπιγράψαντα
source_issues.issue: The accusative participle is syntactically marked with the first-person subject of οὐκ ὤκνησα. It may agree with an understood accusative subject of the dependent infinitives. The nominative ἐπιγράψας would be a conjectural normalization, not an established correction to the supplied reading.

source_issues.source_quote: Κλήμεντος τῶν Πέτρου ἐπιδημίων κηρυγμάτων ἐπιτομή
source_issues.issue: The title renders ἐπιδημίων with the broad adjective sense “among the people,” attested in LSJ under ἐπιδήμιος (including Iliad 24.262 and the resident-merchants usage in Herodotus 2.39). Local or public preaching is a possible contextual emphasis. An association with Peter’s visits is suggested by the preceding city-by-city description, but a specific sojourning sense is not asserted from cognate words alone. These alternatives remain interpretive, not proposed changes to the Greek.

lexical_decisions.chosen: I had made my promise
lexical_decisions.rationale: The participle records Clement’s promise before describing his prompt fulfillment of it.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the greater part
lexical_decisions.rationale: The expression denotes the bulk or most of the material rather than necessarily all of it.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to present in outline
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase concerns reducing or presenting the material by principal points, not merely placing otherwise unabridged material beneath headings.

lexical_decisions.chosen: as a kind of reminder
lexical_decisions.rationale: Literally involving a sign or marker, the phrase describes the summary as an aid to recognition or recollection.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Clement’s Epitome of Peter’s Preachings among the People
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adjective ἐπιδήμιος itself has the LSJ sense “among the people,” with community, local and resident associations. This broader wording avoids deriving a specific sojourning meaning merely from cognate nouns or verbs. The preceding city-by-city account supplies context, not a lexical equation with travel.

lexical_decisions.chosen: set it out
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb marks the transition from the prefatory letter to presenting the promised material.
